text: Git is a version control system that helps developers track changes in their code. One of its key features is branching, which lets you create separate lines of development. A common practice is using feature branches, where you work on a new feature without affecting the main code. When the feature is ready, you merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project organized, reduces mistakes, and allows several people to work at the same time safely.
